title: GATE 2027 Study Plan: 80-Day Preparation Strategy by Paper
summary: GATE 2027 study plan for the 80 days left: four phases, section weightage for ME, CE, EE, EC, negative-marking maths and a mock-test schedule.
body_markdown:
From 18 November 2026 you have 80 days to the first GATE 2027 exam day, 6 February 2027. A plan that fits: 33 days to finish the syllabus, heaviest sections of your paper first; 21 days of revision with previous-year questions; 21 days of 6-7 full mock tests; and a 5-day taper. General Aptitude and engineering mathematics are worth 28 of the 100 marks in ME, CE, EE and EC, so practise them every day from the start. Paper-wise dates are not out yet, so plan for 6 February.


> **GATE 2027 preparation in numbers (as of 18 Nov 2026)**
>
>
> - **Time left:** 80 days to day 1 (6 Feb 2027) and 95 days to the last exam day (21 Feb). Source:[GATE 2027 Important Dates](https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/important_dates) , IIT Madras.
> - **Fixed marks:** General Aptitude 15 and engineering mathematics 13 in ME, CE, EE, EC and IN. That is more than the 2026 General qualifying mark in ME (25.2), EE (27.7) and EC (26.4). Sources:[GATE 2027 brochure](https://gate2027ib.iitm.ac.in/GATE2027-IB.pdf) and[GATE 2026 cut-offs](https://gate2026.iitg.ac.in/cut-off.html) .
> - **Heaviest core sections, 2022-26:** CE structural 19.8 marks per paper; EC analog circuits 10.2; EE power electronics 9.8; ME's three core blocks 23.8-24.2 each. Source: Skill-Lync's solved previous-year question banks (ME 6 papers, CE 10, EE 5, EC 5).
> - **No negative marking:** 43-54% of marks in those papers were MSQ or NAT questions, which lose nothing for a wrong answer. Source: the same Skill-Lync banks.
> - **Still open:** free fixing of application defects until 30 Nov 2026. City slip 4 Jan 2027, result 19 Mar 2027.


This plan is for candidates already registered for GATE 2027 in Mechanical (ME), Civil (CE), Electrical (EE), Electronics and Communication (EC), Instrumentation (IN) or the new Robotics and Automation (RA) paper. It suits a final-year student or a working engineer who has covered the syllabus once but has gaps. If you are starting from zero, the order still holds: you just won't cover every section, so the weightage table matters even more.


## How many days are left for GATE 2027, and what are the key dates?


As of 18 November 2026, 80 days are left to the first exam day. GATE 2027 runs on 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 February 2027, in a forenoon session (9:30 am to 12:30 pm) and an afternoon session (2:30 pm to 5:30 pm). Free rectification of application defects closes on 30 November 2026. The exam city slip is due on 4 January 2027 and the result on 19 March 2027.


Two dates are still "to be announced": the admit card and the paper-wise schedule, which says which paper falls on which day. In 2025 and 2026 the admit card came out 25 days before the first exam. Skill-Lync tracks every official change on the same URLs:[GATE 2027 exam dates](https://skill-lync.com/gate/exam-dates) ,[admit card](https://skill-lync.com/gate/admit-card) and[result and cut-offs](https://skill-lync.com/gate/result) . This article is about what to do with the days in between.


## What is the best GATE 2027 study plan for the 80 days left?


Split the 80 days into four phases: finish the syllabus (18 November to 20 December, 33 days), revise with previous-year questions (21 December to 10 January, 21 days), take full mock tests (11 to 31 January, 21 days), and taper (1 to 5 February). Each phase ends on a fixed date, so you can tell in time if you are falling behind.


The four phases set against the official GATE 2027 dates. The hollow marker is where the admit card would fall if it again came out 25 days before day 1. That is history, not an announcement. Phase Dates Days What to do Done when


1. Finish the syllabus 18 Nov to 20 Dec 2026 33 Fill gaps in your paper's heaviest sections first (next section). One timed GA set and one maths topic every day. Fix any application defect before 30 Nov. Every section studied once, with your own formula sheet for each.


2. Revise with PYQs 21 Dec 2026 to 10 Jan 2027 21 Solve the 2022-2026 questions topic by topic, under a timer. Log every wrong answer with its cause: concept, calculation or misreading. Download the city slip on 4 Jan. Every topic's last five years of questions attempted; the error log sorted by cause.


3. Full mocks 11 to 31 Jan 2027 21 A 3-hour mock every 3 to 4 days on the official virtual calculator. Spend the next day reviewing it and fixing what it exposed. 6 or 7 mocks taken and reviewed. Download the admit card when it is out.


4. Taper 1 to 5 Feb 2027 5 Formula sheets and the error log only. Take two mocks at your paper's session time once the schedule is out. Calm, rested, documents printed.


Phase 2 is deliberately long. A previous-year question shows how GATE frames a topic, and the same core ideas come back year after year. Every one of Skill-Lync's[GATE ME](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical) ,[CE](https://skill-lync.com/gate/civil) and[EE](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electrical) topic pages, and the EC pages such as[analog circuits](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electronics/analog-circuits) , has a worked solution checked against the official key. That makes them easy to use for revision without a coaching book.


## Which sections carry the most marks in my GATE paper?


Over 2022-2026, ME's three core blocks each averaged about 24 marks a paper. CE was led by structural engineering (19.8 marks), then geotechnical (13.9) and water resources (13.0). EE spread its marks evenly, with power electronics on top at 9.8. EC was led by analog circuits (10.2), communications (10.0) and digital circuits (9.6).


Average marks per paper for each core section in Skill-Lync's solved previous-year banks (ME 6 papers, CE 10, EE 5, EC 5). GA and engineering mathematics are left out because they are fixed at 15 and 13 marks. The EE banks miss 1 to 4 marks per paper and the EC banks up to 5, where questions are still being solved.


These are averages over the official papers in Skill-Lync's banks, which are built from the GATE papers and answer keys for 2022-2026. Most syllabi were revised for 2027, so read them as where the marks have fallen, not a promise for February. Use them to choose the order of study, not to decide which sections to drop.


Paper Finish first (avg marks per paper) What the numbers say Practise here


ME Applied mechanics and design 24.2; fluids and thermal 24.0; manufacturing and industrial 23.8 The three blocks are almost equal, so you cannot skip one. Strength of materials alone averaged 10.0 marks, the most of any ME subject.[GATE ME weightage and PYQs](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical) ;[GATE 2027 ME guide](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/gate-2027-mechanical-engineering)


CE Structural 19.8; geotechnical 13.9; water resources 13.0 Structural is the largest block. Environmental (10.9) and transportation (10.0) give a good return for their size. Construction materials and management is a separate section in the 2027 syllabus.[GATE CE PYQs](https://skill-lync.com/gate/civil) ;[CE 2027 syllabus](https://skill-lync.com/gate/civil/syllabus)


EE Power electronics 9.8; power systems 8.8; signals and systems 8.6; analog and digital 8.6 No section reaches 10 marks, so breadth beats depth: each weak section costs about 8 to 10 marks.[GATE EE PYQs](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electrical) ;[EE 2027 syllabus](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electrical/syllabus)


EC Analog circuits 10.2; communications 10.0; digital circuits 9.6 Six sections average between 8.4 and 10.2 marks, so the marks are spread evenly across the paper.[analog](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electronics/analog-circuits) ,[communications](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electronics/communications) and[digital circuits](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electronics/digital-circuits) PYQs


IN No Skill-Lync bank yet. The 2027 syllabus has 10 sections, from measurements and sensors to communication and optical instrumentation. The 2026 General qualifying mark was 39.8, the highest of these five papers, so accuracy matters more than coverage. Official previous papers on the GATE 2027 site


RA Part A (common): 39 questions, 60 marks. Part B: 16 questions, 25 marks, either B1 Electrical or B2 Mechanical, chosen during the exam. A new paper with no past papers. Check the official Mock Test Links page for an RA mock and pick B1 or B2 well before exam day.[GATE 2027 RA guide](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/gate-2027-robotics-and-automation)


## Should I start with General Aptitude and engineering mathematics?


Yes, alongside your core subjects rather than instead of them. In ME, CE, EE, EC and IN, General Aptitude is 15 marks and engineering mathematics 13, for 28 of 100. That is more than the 2026 General qualifying mark in ME, EE and EC. The syllabus for both is short and the questions are predictable.


Paper GA + maths (marks) 2026 General qualifying mark Difference


ME 28 25.2 +2.8


CE 28 28.7 −0.7


EE 28 27.7 +0.3


EC 28 26.4 +1.6


IN 28 39.8 −11.8


Nobody qualifies on GA and maths alone, and qualifying is only the first step: admissions and PSU shortlists rank candidates by score. The table shows why a short daily block on these two pays off: they make up a large, reliable share of the marks you need. RA is different. It has no separate maths section: its 85 subject marks sit in Parts A and B, and GA is the usual 15. Practice questions:[quantitative aptitude](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical/general-aptitude-quantitative) ,[verbal reasoning](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical/general-aptitude-verbal-reasoning) and[linear algebra](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical/linear-algebra) .


## How should I handle negative marking in GATE 2027?


Only multiple-choice questions (MCQs) have negative marking: you lose one third of the question's marks for a wrong answer. Multiple-select (MSQ) and numerical (NAT) questions cost nothing when wrong. In Skill-Lync's 2022-2026 banks, 43-54% of the marks were MSQ or NAT, so always attempt those. Guess an MCQ only after you have ruled out at least one option.

NAT answers are entered as numbers and marked against an answer range in the official key. Rounding and units are therefore where marks leak; practise on the official virtual calculator, not your own.


## How many mock tests should I take before GATE 2027?


About 8 or 9 full-length mocks: 6 or 7 between 11 and 31 January (one every 3 to 4 days), plus 2 in the taper week at your paper's session time. That is 24-27 hours of exam conditions. A proper review takes hours, which is why the plan leaves the day after each mock for it.


Use the official mock test on the GATE 2027 website at least once, so the screen layout, the virtual calculator and the question palette are familiar. A mock is useful only if you review it. For every lost mark, write down whether it was a concept you didn't know, a calculation slip, a misread question or time running out. After three mocks the pattern is often clear, and that pattern decides what you revise, not the syllabus order.


## What if my GATE 2027 paper is on 20 or 21 February?


You then get up to two more weeks. Use them for extra mocks and the error log, not new topics. IIT Madras says the paper-wise schedule will be "notified later" on the GATE 2027 website. Until it is, assume 6 February. The past two schedules put branch papers in different places each year:


Paper GATE 2025 (IIT Roorkee) GATE 2026 (IIT Guwahati)


ME Sun 2 Feb, forenoon Sat 14 Feb, afternoon


CE (two sessions) Sun 16 Feb, both sessions Sat 14 Feb, both sessions


EE Sun 2 Feb, afternoon Sat 14 Feb, forenoon


EC Sat 15 Feb, afternoon Sun 15 Feb, forenoon


IN Sat 1 Feb, afternoon Sat 7 Feb, forenoon


GATE 2027 has six exam days against four in 2025 and 2026, so last year's slot predicts little. If you registered for two papers, for example ME with RA, which the brochure's tentative Table 4 allows, you will write them in two sessions. Keep both syllabi warm until the schedule is out.


If a weak subject is weak because the concept never clicked, a short course can help more than another question set. Skill-Lync's[thermodynamics foundations](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/foundations-thermodynamics-industrial-applications) ,[RCC design](https://skill-lync.com/civil-engineering-courses/reinforced-cement-concrete-design) and[power electronics](https://skill-lync.com/electrical-engineering-courses/power-electronics-ev-applications) courses teach the same ideas through industry examples. If you are weighing GATE against a core job,[career options after engineering](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/high-paying-career-options-after-engineering) sets the paths side by side.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is 80 days enough to prepare for GATE 2027?


It is enough to revise a syllabus you have studied before and to take 8 or 9 full mocks. It is tight for learning most of a paper from scratch. In that case, study in order of weightage, keep GA and maths daily, and accept that one or two low-weight sections may get only previous-year-question practice.


### How do I prepare for GATE in 3 months while in final year or working?


Protect a fixed daily block and use weekends for the long tasks: full mocks, topic tests and error-log reviews. The exam days are all Saturdays and Sundays, so weekend mocks also match the real timing. Cut phase 1 to the heaviest sections of your paper and lean on previous-year questions in phase 2.


### Should I solve previous-year questions or take mock tests first?


Previous-year questions first, topic by topic, then full mocks. Topic-wise questions show you what GATE asks and where your concepts are weak. Full mocks test speed, stamina and question choice, which only help once the concepts are in place.


### Which subject should I start with for GATE ME?


Strength of materials averaged 10.0 marks per ME paper over 2022-2026 in Skill-Lync's banks, the most of any subject. Machining and metrology came next at 8.8, then fluid mechanics at 8.5. The three core blocks are nearly equal overall, so start with your weakest heavy subject, not the one you like.


### How do I prepare for the GATE 2027 Robotics and Automation paper with no past papers?


Work from the official syllabus. Part A (60 marks) is common to everyone; Part B is either Electrical or Mechanical, 25 marks, chosen during the exam. Use ME or EE previous-year questions for the topics that overlap, and check the official Mock Test Links page for an RA mock. The[GATE 2027 RA guide](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/gate-2027-robotics-and-automation) maps the overlap.
